author: Akien
prose:
THE SLEEP TRIGGER — captured across three turns of one design conversation, 2026-08-06, in order and verbatim.

(1) Raising it, from the question of who owns the evening run:

"yes, the evening run. we don't have an owner for it. and as we move into actual graph tree reasoning, we will need things to do consolidation and whatnot, yes? so many parts of the system may well eventually need 'overnight runs' and the learning blocks: they have a candidate questions entry. where do you think those question come from? has to be either an llm escalation, or an LLM enabled (at LEAST thru escalation) overnight run. so... how do we want to handle that? option one, each device class or device instance can post whatever it needs to it's own heartbeat reciever... or could be same for the whole system in the system object... but we've said that represents the hardware and software on the box. do we need another device that's 'the whole cairn system as a representation?' use the skelleton? something else? What do you think? What would be the best way?"

and in the same turn, on false positives:

"yes, and everything that has one of these should have a learning loop to improve it. because that's the only way out."

(2) Correcting the predicate away from the clock:

"almost. during the day, the box will be busy with the humans, at night not. it's not about a specific hour, it's about when other external things won't trouble it. How's that?"

(3) Naming it:

"then let's call it the 'sleep' trigger. anything that i say 'overnight' about is really about this. we could put the system into a '3 hours without a human' screensaver like trigger"
